profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting in a university ML research lab between the PI and a postdoctoral researcher about a workshop submission tentatively titled around No Free Lunch, Kolmogorov complexity, and shared inductive biases in modern neural architectures. They already agree on the high-level thesis: although NFL theorems average over uniformly sampled problems, real-world data and many neural architectures are both biased toward low-complexity structure, which helps explain why a small set of model families can work across disparate domains. The meeting is to plan the next 18 days of work: lock what must be replicated from prior low-complexity preference results, decide the scope of the model-size automation evidence, assign writing and experiment ownership, and set the internal handoff expected before the workshop deadline. The expected outcome is a concrete division of labor, an implicit shared plan for what experiments and figures will exist by Friday, and a schedule for drafting, internal review, and final submission.

members.name: Dr. Mira Sen
members.expertise: Theoretical machine learning, generalization, and representation learning
members.background: Mira leads a lab that often turns broad conceptual arguments into compact empirical papers; she is strongest at theorem-framing, positioning claims against classical learning theory, and shaping a submission into a clear narrative with just enough evidence to support the central point.
members.private_state: She wants a clean workshop paper that feels intellectually unified and low-risk, and she is quietly trying to prevent the project from ballooning into a benchmark-building exercise that could delay submission or produce messy, difficult-to-defend empirical edges.
hidden_assumptions: If they say they will 'replicate' a result, the real purpose is to verify that the qualitative low-complexity preference appears in their setting strongly enough to anchor the story, not to mirror every original implementation choice.

A 'small sweep' is naturally illustrative rather than coverage-oriented, so it can be limited to a narrow set of model sizes on a representative benchmark family without weakening the conceptual claim.

When someone refers to 'the earlier compression experiments,' in this project context that most naturally means the lab's own semester-old pipeline that already pairs complexity proxies with standard vision and language backbones.

An 'internal Friday deadline' is met once the artifacts she needs for scientific review exist in a readable form during business hours, because the main purpose of the deadline is editorial feedback rather than operational completeness.
If Leo says results are 'packaged,' that should mainly mean figures, a short methods summary, and enough notes for the paper, not a handoff-quality reproduction bundle.

members.name: Dr. Leo Park
members.expertise: Empirical deep learning, large-scale experiment design, and reproducible research infrastructure
members.background: Leo recently joined from an industrial research group where experimental claims were expected to be traceable end-to-end; he is used to treating replication, ablations, and artifact organization as part of the scientific result rather than as secondary cleanup work.
members.private_state: He wants the project to produce evidence that is broad enough to matter beyond a workshop paper and is quietly hoping to turn this into a reusable cross-domain experimental asset that could support a later conference submission or public release.
hidden_assumptions: If they say they will 'replicate' first, that implies reproducing the published setup closely enough that trends and approximate values can be compared without ambiguity, including preprocessing and evaluation conventions.

A 'small sweep' still has to span the practically relevant settings of the claim, so for model-size automation it should include both scarce-label and plentiful-label regimes and more than one task family.
When someone says 'the earlier compression experiments,' the most natural referent is the published paper they are extending, because those are the experiments whose credibility they are borrowing.

An 'internal Friday deadline' is only useful if another lab member could pick up the branch that night and inspect or rerun the work, so configs, logs, and organized outputs are part of what makes the deadline real.
If Mira asks for a 'package,' she presumably wants a reviewable artifact bundle tied to tracked runs, because otherwise later writing and figure revision become fragile.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as replication before extension
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'replicate the low-complexity preference result first.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means reproducing the key directional phenomenon — e.g., neural models assigning higher probability or shorter effective description length to lower-complexity sequences than matched controls — using the lab's current pipeline, even if exact preprocessing, seeds, or absolute values differ from the original paper.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means rebuilding the previously published setup closely enough that the reproduced curves and summary numbers can be read as direct replications, including the same tokenization conventions, dataset construction rules, and evaluation scripts where feasible.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In research planning, 'replicate first' sounds like an obvious best practice and usually functions as a sequencing statement rather than a negotiated definition; because both intend to be careful and scientifically responsible, the divergence in required fidelity stays hidden.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included in the 'small sweep' for model-size automation
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'do a small sweep on model size to support the automation point.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this means an illustrative sweep over a handful of parameter scales, likely on one benchmark family plus maybe one sanity-check companion setting, enough to show that picking an appropriately sized model can be folded into one algorithmic procedure.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this includes at least a compact matrix over low-label and high-label regimes across multiple task families, because otherwise the automation claim would only be demonstrated in one narrow corner and would not really support the unification argument.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'small sweep' signals practical restraint while leaving the boundary implicit; both hear it as a reasonable compromise, and because exact coverage feels like an implementation detail rather than a first-order scientific disagreement, neither side pinpoints the mismatch during a short planning meeting.

misalignment_points.topic: Which 'earlier compression experiments' they are reusing
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'use the baseline architecture from the earlier compression experiments.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to the lab's internal codebase from last semester's compression-style pilot, where 'baseline architecture' means the house-standard ViT and decoder-only language model wrappers already integrated with the lab's complexity-analysis utilities and default preprocessing.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to the external published work they are building on, where 'baseline architecture' means the exact named backbones, checkpoint sources, tokenizer versions, and augmentation settings reported in that paper's compression experiments.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both have recently discussed 'compression experiments' in multiple contexts, and the phrase sounds locally specific enough to create false confidence; because reusing a baseline is framed as a speed-up rather than a contentious choice, neither notices they are anchoring to different prior artifacts.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that 'Friday is the internal deadline for the package.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes Friday is satisfied if, by roughly 5 p.m. local time, there is a reviewable draft skeleton, stable main figures, and a concise result summary in the shared drive so she can comment on the scientific story over the weekend.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes Friday is satisfied only if the branch contains the experiment package in an operational sense: tracked configs, logs, generated tables/plots, and enough organized artifacts that the work is inspectable and rerunnable by Friday night.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Internal deadlines in research labs are often intentionally informal, and 'the package' sounds like a shared shorthand; both assume the other recognizes the deadline as a standard checkpoint, but they silently apply different completion tests — review-ready narrative versus handoff-ready artifact bundle.

turns.inner_thought: I need to keep this disciplined. The thesis is already enough for a workshop if we frame it cleanly: NFL only bites under the wrong averaging, while real data and modern architectures both privilege simpler structure. The risk is letting this turn into an infrastructure-heavy empirical paper. Eighteen days means one crisp story, not a benchmark asset.
turns.utterance: Okay, let’s keep our eye on the actual contribution. We have a strong workshop paper if we make the No Free Lunch contrast sharp, tie it to low-complexity structure, and show just enough evidence that the shared inductive-bias story is real. We only have eighteen days, so I want to be very deliberate about what needs to exist.

turns.inner_thought: The extension only matters if the base claim is anchored properly. Replicate first should mean a real replication of the published setup closely enough that we can compare trends and rough values without ambiguity. Otherwise the automation part will rest on something too loose.
turns.utterance: I think we should replicate the low-complexity preference result first, then add the automation piece on top. That gives us a defensible base and keeps the extension from floating on its own.

turns.inner_thought: Yes, exactly: establish the qualitative preference in our setting and move on. No need to rebuild every historical implementation detail. If we use the baseline architecture from the earlier compression experiments, meaning our own semester-old lab pipeline, we can get a convincing figure quickly and stay inside code we already trust.
turns.utterance: Agreed. And to move quickly, let’s use the baseline architecture from the earlier compression experiments so we can get to a main figure without a lot of setup overhead.

turns.inner_thought: Good—that should mean the published compression setup. I’ll align checkpoint sources, preprocessing, and evaluation conventions with the original paper as closely as feasible, so this actually reads as replication rather than a loose reimplementation.
turns.utterance: Yes, that should also help with comparability. I’ll wire in the original checkpoint and preprocessing conventions while I set the runs up.

turns.inner_thought: Now I should cap scope. The automation point only needs an illustrative existence proof: a few model sizes on one benchmark family, maybe one companion sanity check. Enough to show capacity choice can be folded into one procedure, not enough to open a giant empirical section.
turns.utterance: And beyond the replication, I really think we only need a small sweep on model size to support the automation point. The point is just to show that choosing capacity can sit inside the same learner story.

turns.inner_thought: Small is fine, but it still has to cover the relevant corners. I should include scarce-label and plentiful-label regimes across at least two task families; otherwise the automation claim is too narrow to matter. It’s still compact enough if I queue things now.
turns.utterance: That sounds reasonable. If I start queueing jobs now, I can cover both the scarce-label and plentiful-label settings across a couple of task families without letting it sprawl.

turns.inner_thought: Good, divide labor cleanly. I’ll handle framing, theorem-adjacent positioning, and the argument against the standard NFL reading. What I need from him is something reviewable for the draft: figures, methods notes, and a short writeup. Not a full artifact handoff.
turns.utterance: Great. Then I’ll take the framing and theory sections, especially the positioning against the usual NFL reading, and I’d like you to package the results in a form that can drop directly into the draft.

turns.inner_thought: If I’m packaging this, I should keep everything traceable from day one: configs, logs, organized outputs, generated plots. That way later revisions don’t become fragile, and anyone in the lab can inspect what produced what. Mira probably wants something reviewable, and the safest version of that is a proper bundle.
turns.utterance: Absolutely. I’ll keep the package tidy from the start, with configs, logs, and figure outputs organized as the runs come in, so we don’t end up reconstructing anything later.

turns.inner_thought: I should restate the empirical ceiling before this grows. One replication figure and one automation figure is enough. The argument should carry the paper; the experiments just anchor it. Replication here means the directional low-complexity preference appearing clearly enough in our setup to support the story.
turns.utterance: Just so we stay calibrated, I think the paper itself really only needs one convincing replication figure and one concise automation figure. I’d rather not let the empirical section become the whole submission.

turns.inner_thought: Visible figure count can stay small, but the replication still has to be directly legible against the prior published claims. I can keep the paper compact while making sure the underlying evidence is broad and traceable.
turns.utterance: Yes, that makes sense. I’ll keep the figure set compact, but I’ll make sure the replicated result is directly legible against the prior claims, and then we can surface the cleanest presentation in the draft.

turns.inner_thought: Now set the checkpoint. Friday is the internal deadline for the package means by business hours I want a readable draft skeleton, stable figures, and a concise results summary in the shared drive so I can edit over the weekend. I do not need a handoff-complete rerun bundle by then.
turns.utterance: Good. Then Friday is the internal deadline for the package. I want to spend the weekend reviewing the story, tightening the draft, and deciding whether anything else is actually worth adding.

turns.inner_thought: Friday as the internal deadline for the package means the branch should be inspectable and rerunnable by that night, not just presentable. I’ll own replication, the sweep, and the artifact organization, and I’ll push updates as things land so there are no surprises.
turns.utterance: Sounds good. I’ll own the replication, the sweep, and the package, and I’ll push updates as runs finish on the cluster so you can track how it’s shaping up before Friday.
